summary: The user reported that a stream visible in a browser becomes black when switching back to the Android client. SurfaceTextureRenderer previously ignored SurfaceProducer.onSurfaceAvailable and could reacquire a surface before Flutter announced it was restored. Rendering is now gated between cleanup and availability callbacks; after resume, the renderer reacquires the current surface on the next frame. This is a lifecycle fix candidate, not yet confirmed as the cause of the remote black stream.

checks.observation: The state starts available, blocks rendering after cleanup, and permits rendering after onSurfaceAvailable.

checks.name: User-started Pixel app-only foreground transition
checks.observation: The user confirmed they started this test. Read-only ADB initially showed MediaProjection actively recording the Calculator task, the BOOHTACORD process alive with its foreground MediaProjection service, and Calculator in the foreground. Chrome SHARE_TEST then showed one participant and zero screen-share publications; Pistol121_android was absent. After BOOHTACORD returned to foreground, Chrome showed two participants again, but zero publications, and ADB showed no active MediaProjection. On a later read-only snapshot, BOOHTACORD was foreground with no active MediaProjection and no app foreground service; the user has not clarified whether they intentionally stopped capture. No screen content was captured and the agent did not stop the test. Thus the room participant loss/recovery was observed, but there is no retained publication with which to prove a decoder black frame or assign who stopped capture.

limitations: A successful SurfaceProducer lifecycle unit test does not prove the actual Flutter compositor displays resumed frames.

Android's selected-app projection was active while its participant/publication disappeared from the browser roster; the participant returned after app resume while capture was already stopped. The cause and whether the stop was user-initiated remain unconfirmed.

Android's official app-screen-sharing behavior says the selected app's captured region becomes invisible when another app entirely covers it or the user navigates away. If this report is about Calculator app-only capture while BOOHTACORD is foreground, a black remote image may be expected privacy behavior; this does not explain a black image during full-display capture or while the selected app remains visible. Source: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/media/projection/MediaProjection.Callback#onCapturedContentVisibilityChanged(boolean).

The test used selected-app Calculator capture, not full-display capture. Receiver-side decoded-frame counters for a still-published track were unavailable because the browser showed no active publication.
remaining: Clarify whether the user stopped the capture. For a new authorized run, keep BOOHTACORD joined, transition between Calculator and BOOHTACORD without pressing stop, and monitor room membership, MediaProjection state, sender encoded frames and receiver decoded frames. For app-only capture, verify that the selected app is visible and treat Android's privacy masking while it is covered/navigated away as expected; repeat with full-display capture to isolate lifecycle/rendering defects. Consider explaining this limitation in the source picker. Keep FE-59 and FE-64 open until resumed preview, room persistence and paired browser playback pass.
